messages:
Nina T: Heads-up: onboarding CS reported a failing quickstart. They copied the README curl and got a 401 with 'insufficient_scope'.
Oliver R: Oof. Which README? quickstart or sample-app README?
Nina T: Quickstart (top-level README under 'Make your first request'). They pasted exactly: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1","input":"hi"}'
```
Priya M: Two likely issues: (1) new scoped keys require inference.write for POST, (2) our sample-app env var name sometimes shows as REDWOOD_KEY in codebases. Copy/paste mismatch.
Nina T: CS says their CI rotates keys mid-run and then the next request fails with: `{"error":"insufficient_scope"}`. Logs show: `auth: token present but missing scope: inference.write`.
Oliver R: Ok that's definitely a docs drift thing. README should call out required scopes and recommended token type (short-lived user vs service token) so people hit fewer surprises.
Priya M: Also SDK parity: Node quickstart mentions automatic retries for auth errors, but Python snippet doesn't show how to refresh or retry. Users copying the Python example hit the rotation-case more often.
CI Bot: docs-ci: linkcheck passed; spellcheck found 'REDDWOOD_API_KEY' typo in sample-app README line 42.
Nina T: Yikes. Can we do a small patch: (A) small 'Auth troubleshooting' note under quickstart listing common 401 messages and fixes, (B) change example curl to include a comment about scope, (C) fix sample app env var to use REDWOOD_API_KEY everywhere, (D) add a one-liner pointer to SDK retry docs for long-running jobs.
Oliver R: I'll open a tiny PR for (A)(B)(C). Will add the comment above the curl: `# Make sure your key includes the inference.write scope or use a service token`.
Priya M: I'll add a short Python snippet for retries/refresh to the "Advanced" section. Example: 
```python
# simple backoff + retry example using requests' Retry for transient 5xx/429
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from urllib3.util.retry import Retry
retry = Retry(total=4, backoff_factor=0.2, status_forcelist=[429,500,502,503,504])
session.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retry))
# or set client.retry = retry in SDK if available
```
Priya M: Also suggest a tiny test in samples: CI smoke test that runs quickstart with a dummy rotate to ensure we see a descriptive error, that'll catch regressions.
QA Bot: qa: added checklist item to sample-app smoke tests: validate env var presence and expected 401 error messaging.
Nina T: Can we also add a single-line changelog entry at top of README: "2026-02-12: clarified auth scopes and env var names" so support can quickly reference.
Oliver R: Yep. I'll tag @Priya M on the PR for the snippet review.
Nina T: Thanks. Leaving this open until PR merged. :thumbsup:
